purpose: Separate the professional buyer-side acquisition strategy report from certification and audit artifacts, while preserving decision-grade investment committee usefulness.

main_report.audience: deal team, investment committee, strategy reviewer
main_report.style: professional buyer-side acquisition strategy analysis, suitable for management / investment committee / board review
allowed_content: buyer strategic objectives and why-buy analysis
transaction timing and why-now analysis inside deal logic
target business or asset quality assessment
strategic fit and value creation thesis
financial analysis where source-backed inputs exist
valuation status, price justification, and unavailable-data caveats
synergy status and quantified synergy only when certified
diligence gaps written as business questions
100-day integration or development plan where relevant
final acquisition recommendation, red lines, and next actions
forbidden_content: machine certification jargon in the body

business_translation_rules.audit_input: Certified or Certified with Caveat claim
business_translation_rules.main_report_output: Business fact or caveated business statement without exposing the internal claim ID.

business_translation_rules.audit_input: Needs Human Review or Not Certified claim
business_translation_rules.main_report_output: Open diligence item or excluded conclusion; do not use it as recommendation support.
Human-readable source description only when needed; keep raw IDs in report_manifest.json.
Deal economics sentence, sensitivity table, or unavailable-data note in investor-facing language.

main_report_must_answer_decision_questio: at what price or why price is not certified
can the buyer win with the asset
how should deal risk be shared
proceed / proceed with conditions / renegotiate / defer / walk away

runner_guidance: Treat the current mandate, current-case files, and current-case research as the only source of company identities, transaction facts, model inputs, and conclusions; never reuse prior-case content.
Select and document methods from current-case business model, asset maturity, cash-flow profile, transaction type, control objective, and available evidence. No single model is globally mandatory.
Generate the professional report from business-facing supporting materials and certified analysis objects, not by dumping the claim ledger.
Use the structured judgment chain only as an internal reasoning and quality-control mechanism. Never print its field names as a repeated report template.
Synthesize the validated objects into the original report's natural section logic, business prose, calculations, and appropriate tables; the main report must not explain the runner or its schema.
Before synthesis, test the strongest counter-thesis, assumptions, cross-module dependencies, and explicit decision thresholds for every major section.
Run quality control before rendering; the renderer must not create business judgments, conditions, diligence actions, or 100-day workstreams.
Do not write the main report as a list of facts plus caveats. Each major section must convert facts into buyer-side implication and decision impact.
When evidence is incomplete, explain what bounded business judgment is still supported and how the missing evidence affects price, structure, financing, risk, or recommendation.
Keep raw audit IDs and certification mechanics in manifest and audit package files.
If the only available material is an audit ledger, first translate it into business-facing analysis objects before drafting the report.
Do not replace the buyer-side acquisition strategy report framework with a separate IC memo template. Improve the original framework by making each module decision-grade.
Do not let a strategic rationale substitute for an investment decision. The report must state whether price, timing, structure, valuation, and recommendation are certified or restricted.

If valuation, comparable transactions, competitive differentiation, or price ceiling cannot be certified, write that limitation plainly in the main memo instead of implying a clean proceed recommendation.
If translation would overstate evidence, emit a restricted output or research gap memo instead of a polished recommendation.
Fail closed when the authoritative case analysis is missing; do not infer recommendations from filenames, file presence, row counts, keyword matches, or certification status alone.
Use tables only when they compare alternatives, expose assumptions, replay calculations, allocate risk, or change the decision. Do not preserve empty tables to satisfy a count.

When current-case evidence identifies a clinical-stage biopharma asset, replace operating-company EBITDA templates with indication-level rNPV and explicit clinical, regulatory, IP, CMC, market, financing, and milestone analysis; otherwise select the applicable sector/transaction adapter.
Separate decision-date evidence, later primary-source disclosure of historical facts, and post-decision outcomes. Never present hindsight as contemporaneous diligence.
